what_it_is: oh-my-openagent (OmO) is a large TypeScript/Rust monorepo of multi-harness agent plugins (OpenCode, Codex, and the senpi/Pi harness) that adds orchestration, memory, skills, and continuation hooks on top of a host coding agent. Its 'mass-ulw' feature is a journaled dependency-graph engine (packages/senpi-task/src/dag) that compiles node graphs, admits nodes on a dependency frontier, writes every transition to a filesystem WAL, and supports retry/amend/send recovery and resume after restart. Around it sit prompt-level contracts (ulw-loop, ulw-execute, ulw-plan skills) for goals, binary success criteria, evidence and checkpoints, plus hook components that inject a 'TREAT AS FALSE UNTIL YOU PROVE IT' directive, force authorization questions to block, guard spawns, and auto-continue unfinished work. Most completion authority still rests on agent-authored evidence, self-reported child status, and approval-biased LLM reviewers, so its engineering (fingerprints, transitive invalidation, crash safety, path containment) transfers to G1 far better than its verification model. Static review only at commit 0deecd94 (2026-10-11); Sustainable Use License.
architecture: DAG engine: compile, fingerprint, WAL journal, file store, frontier scheduler, retry/send/amend, recovery, results, skill manifest (packages/senpi-task/src/dag)
Task manager: owner-keyed exactly-once child launch, residency cap, steering engine (packages/senpi-task/src/manager/manager.ts)
Completion notifications carrying the TREAT AS FALSE directive (packages/senpi-task/src/completion)
Agent policy: invocation guard (plan gate), one-shot interaction policies, builtin gate-reviewer prompt (packages/senpi-task/src/agents)
Spawn policy composition used by task and DAG paths (packages/senpi-task/src/tools/task/spawn-policy.ts)
omo-senpi task component: workflow tool, DAG runtime composition root, RPC bridge/handlers, wake, verification-context re-selection, advisory lint (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task)
Question gates: force required:true on Approval/Authorize questions (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/question-gates)

Continuation: ulw-execute idle-turn continuation with terminal-outcome gate; ulw-loop footer/continuation (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ulw-execute-continuation, packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ulw-loop)
Memory path guard (soft tool_call guard) and host filesystem policy (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/memory/guard.ts, policy-guard.ts)

Codex ulw-loop plugin: UserPromptSubmit steering, PreToolUse spawn guards, Stop auto-resume, goal/criteria/evidence SDK, quality-gate validator, revision log (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop)
Codex Stop/SubagentStop gates: ulw-execute continuation and executor evidence-receipt gate (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-execute-continuation, lazycodex-executor-verify)
OpenCode goal hook replacing the deprecated token-based ralph-loop (packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/goal, packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/ralph-loop)

Doctrine skills: mass-ulw (+ references/planning.md), dag-library, ulw-loop (+ define-goal, full-workflow), ulw-plan, ulw-execute (packages/omo-senpi/skills, packages/shared-skills/skills/ulw-execute)
Docs: mass-ulw viewer protocol and orchestration guide (docs/reference/mass-ulw-protocol.md, docs/guide/orchestration.md)
Boulder state: plan checklist grammar and stale-work demotion (packages/boulder-state/src)

Not read (out of focus or large/generated): CHANGELOG.md (682 KB), changes.md (430 KB), bun.lock, Cargo.lock, crates/ (Rust native), packages/oh-my-opencode-* platform binary packages, packages/web, bundled sdk.js (packages/omo-senpi/plugin/runtime/agent-toolkit-sdk/sdk.js), memory/computer-use/telemetry internals

atoms.name: Deterministic graph compile rejects cycles and dangling deps
atoms.statement: Every DAG definition is compiled purely and deterministically, and any invalid id, duplicate, unknown or self dependency, cycle, size-cap breach, or empty graph is fatal, so no run is created.
atoms.mechanism: compileDag validates ids, duplicates, unknown/self deps, prompt-byte and fan-out caps, then a peel-off cycle finder reports each cycle deterministically from its lexicographically smallest member (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/graph.ts:155-263, :109-153). Any error returns ok:false and startRun throws invalid_definition before writing a checkpoint, key, or event (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.ts:358-367).
principle_conflict: P2: applied to agy subagent graphs it would duplicate native orchestration; apply only to G1 contract and check graphs
atoms.proof_purpose: The registered contract-dependency graph (contract->contract and criterion->check edges) is closed (every dependency exists) and acyclic, so a completion order exists.
atoms.g1_design: (b) BUILD at contract level: at registration G1 compiles the contract's dependency list against contracts already in the ledger plus the intra-contract check dependency list, rejects unknown/self/cyclic edges with a deterministic cycle listing, and stores the canonical edge set inside the contract hash. No scheduling logic for agy subagents.

atoms.name: Canonical JSON SHA-256 identity fingerprints
atoms.statement: Identity hashes are computed over canonical JSON with sorted keys and omitted undefined values, with set-like arrays normalized and sequence arrays kept ordered.
atoms.mechanism: canonicalize() sorts object keys and drops undefined; nodeFingerprintInput sorts dependsOn and dagDefinitionFingerprint sorts nodes by id before sha256 (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/fingerprint.ts:39-68). Tests pin key-order invariance, array-order sensitivity, and whitespace sensitivity (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/fingerprint.test.ts:42-147).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with a contract hash
atoms.proof_purpose: Two semantically identical contracts hash identically, and any byte change to a proof-bearing field changes the hash.
atoms.g1_design: Keep T1's contract hash but specify canonicalization explicitly: sorted keys, undefined omitted, set-like arrays (dependencies, scope globs) sorted, sequence arrays (check argv) preserved; add golden-hash tests.

atoms.name: Gate semantics version folded into identity hash
atoms.statement: The engine's own semantics (admission policy, failure policy, data policy) are hashed into every definition fingerprint, so a semantics change deliberately prevents reuse of results produced under old rules.
atoms.mechanism: SCHEDULER_FINGERPRINT_INPUT is part of every definition fingerprint; the switch from strict-barrier to dependency-frontier changed all fingerprints so old runs are not reused (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.ts:46-53, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/fingerprint.ts:19-29, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:42).
atoms.proof_purpose: A receipt is reusable only if it was produced by the same G1 gate/verifier semantics version that currently decides completion.
atoms.g1_design: Every receipt carries a G1 semantics digest (verifier code digest plus receipt schema version); the completion predicate rejects receipts whose digest differs from the running G1, forcing re-verification after any G1 upgrade.

atoms.name: Identity hash excludes advisory dispatch material
atoms.statement: The fingerprint covers only the submitted definition, never skill content or effective prompts, so guidance edits do not invalidate results while definition edits do.
atoms.mechanism: effectivePrompt and skill digests are stored separately and excluded from fingerprints; a load_skills-only amendment re-runs nothing (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.ts:166-172, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/fingerprint.ts:10-11, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:49, packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/SKILL.md:83).
principle_conflict: Z5: if a check command or criterion were classed as advisory it would escape the hash; the split must be conservative
atoms.proof_purpose: Receipt validity depends only on proof-bearing inputs (criteria, check argv, env spec, scope, upstream receipts), not on injected prose.
atoms.g1_design: Split the contract record into a hashed proof core (criteria, check argv, env spec, write scope, dependencies) and an unhashed advisory part (rule text, hints) whose digests are logged separately (see OMO-26).

atoms.name: Fingerprint diff with transitive dependent invalidation
atoms.statement: On amendment each node fingerprint is diffed, and changed or added nodes plus all their transitive dependents are reset while unchanged completed nodes keep cached results.
atoms.mechanism: diffNodeFingerprints buckets unchanged/changed/added/removed (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/fingerprint.ts:84-124); amendRun BFS-walks edges from changed+added seeds and resets those nodes to pending with execAttempt+1, dropping outputs (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.ts:487-534, :661-673). The node fingerprint holds only dependency ids, not upstream fingerprints (fingerprint.ts:6-17), so soundness depends on the traversal.
atoms.proof_purpose: A dependent contract's receipt was computed against the current version of every upstream contract and receipt; any upstream change provably invalidates it.
atoms.g1_design: (b) BUILD, improved: make G1 receipt keys Merkle-style, including the receipt hashes of all upstream contracts, so an upstream amendment or re-verification changes the key and invalidates dependents by construction; the same rule applies inside a contract when a check consumes another check's output (build -> test). Keep a traversal only to report which contracts became pending.

atoms.name: Write-ahead amendments with total no-throw reducers
atoms.statement: Because the WAL is written before the reducer runs, reducers never throw; a stale precondition makes the event a replay-safe no-op and the writer detects the lost race from an unadvanced fingerprint.
atoms.mechanism: amendRun re-checks running/scheduled nodes, active run, live lease, and key change, appends, then reads the checkpoint back and reports run_still_active if the fingerprint did not advance (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.ts:491-505, :559-577). applyDagRunMutation returns the record unchanged when any precondition fails (manager.ts:596-613); a test replays a hostile checkpoint without wedging (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.test.ts:619).
atoms.proof_purpose: Every ledger event replays deterministically, a durable but invalid event can never wedge state, and a lost race is detected from the ledger head rather than process memory.
atoms.g1_design: G1 ledger reducers are total: an amendment or receipt event whose expected contract hash or expected head no longer holds is applied as a recorded no-op, and the writer confirms success by reading the advanced head; amendments are refused while a verification for that contract is in flight.

atoms.name: Completed work immutable: amend, never retry
atoms.statement: A completed node cannot be retried and a completed or cancelled run cannot be revived; re-running finished work requires an explicit definition amendment.
atoms.mechanism: assertRetryable refuses completed nodes with 'amend the definition to re-run it' (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/node-retry.ts:163-176); sendToDagNode refuses steer/revive on completed or cancelled runs as settled evidence (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/node-send.ts:44-57).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with a contract hash
atoms.proof_purpose: A completion receipt is never mutated in place; re-opening work leaves the old receipt intact and creates a superseding contract version.
atoms.g1_design: Already in T1; keep: re-opening a completed contract creates a new version referencing the old hash and never edits the completed record.

atoms.name: Retry re-arms dependents; ancestors in same set
atoms.statement: Retrying failed nodes bumps an execution counter, returns cascade-skipped dependents to blocked, and refuses retrying a skipped node unless its failed ancestor is in the same retry set; retry is refused while the run is active.
atoms.mechanism: retryDagNodes journals dag.node.retried with execAttempt+1 and transitions skipped dependents to blocked (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/node-retry.ts:74-135, :146-161); assertRetryable names blocking ancestors (node-retry.ts:163-199); run_still_active guard (node-retry.ts:79-87).
principle_conflict: P8: a separate retry verb is unnecessary when contract state is derived from receipts
atoms.proof_purpose: A downstream contract re-enters only when every upstream it depends on has a current receipt, so no downstream receipt is computed over a still-failed upstream.
atoms.g1_design: (b) derived only: G1 stores no retry/skip states; eligibility of a dependent contract is computed from upstream receipts, and G1 refuses to verify a dependent whose upstream lacks a current receipt.

atoms.name: Receipt-gated dependency admission for native subagents
atoms.statement: A node is admitted only when every node it depends on is completed (dependency-frontier admission), with waves purely informational.
atoms.mechanism: admitFrontier schedules nodes whose dependsOn all hold completed and a residency slot is free; compiled waves never gate execution (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/scheduler.ts:524-569, :577-646, :927-931; packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:30).
principle_conflict: P2: building a scheduler would duplicate agy invoke_subagent and teamwork; G1 may only gate admission
atoms.proof_purpose: Work on contract C started only after G1 receipts existed for every contract C depends on.
atoms.g1_design: (a) GOVERN: when agy spawns a subagent or teamwork lane bound to contract C, the PreToolUse hook denies the call unless the ledger holds current G1 receipts for all of C's upstream contracts; otherwise it prints nothing so native behavior applies. Lane-to-contract binding in hook stdin must be measured on agy first.

atoms.name: Derived failure propagation via quiescent skip cascade
atoms.statement: A waiting node whose dependency ended in any non-completed terminal state is marked skipped, but only when nothing is in flight, so revivable failures are not stranded prematurely.
atoms.mechanism: applyDependentSkipCascade runs only at frontier quiescence and loops to a fixpoint (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/scheduler.ts:536-556, :901-925); an all-failed admission pass re-enters the loop so the cascade can settle the run instead of parking it forever (scheduler.ts:549-555; packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:31).
atoms.proof_purpose: A contract whose upstream failed provably cannot complete, so no Stop continuation is spent on it.
atoms.g1_design: (b) derived, no stored state: at Stop and SessionStart G1 computes 'blocked by failed upstream' from the ledger and excludes those contracts from continuation targets; they become eligible automatically when the upstream gets a fresh receipt.

atoms.name: Node completion equals child self-report
atoms.statement: A DAG node becomes 'completed' whenever its child task ends with status completed, including a child that reports being blocked.
atoms.mechanism: foldTaskOutcome maps TaskRecord.status 'completed' directly to a succeeded transition (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/scheduler.ts:888-899); the planning doctrine admits a node counts as completed even when its response reports being blocked (packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/references/planning.md:170).
principle_conflict: P4: completion decided by the child, not deterministic verification
Z1: trusts the agent
Z4: trusts agent output
P5: no receipt binding
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 never maps an agy subagent, branch, or arm 'done' status to contract completion; only G1 receipts complete contracts.

atoms.name: TREAT AS FALSE directive on completions
atoms.statement: Every model-facing DAG completion notification and run-settle wake carries a directive telling the parent to treat the node summary as a fabricated claim until it re-derives scope and checks artifacts itself.
atoms.mechanism: buildCompletionMessage appends DAG_VERIFICATION_DIRECTIVE when any detail carries a dag owner (packages/senpi-task/src/completion/notification.ts:62-74, packages/senpi-task/src/completion/dag-verification-directive.ts:4-11); run-settle wakes append it as well (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-wake.ts:134-139).
principle_conflict: P4: a prompt directive proves nothing
P8: no proof-bearing purpose in the authority path
atoms.proof_purpose: none (measurement lane only)
atoms.g1_design: Measurement only: A/B-test (ensembles, confidence intervals) whether a PostToolUse or PreInvocation note saying 'subagent results are unverified claims; G1 verifies' lowers Gemini's false-DONE rate; never part of the authority path.

atoms.name: Model-conditional weakening of verification instructions
atoms.statement: The verification directive is swapped for a weaker spot-check variant when the receiver model is GPT-6 Astra, justified only by a comment about that model's prior.
atoms.mechanism: ASTRA variants are chosen by isGpt6AstraModel at notification time and re-selected at every model-call boundary (packages/senpi-task/src/completion/dag-verification-directive.ts:13-21, packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-verification-context.ts:18-62, packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/parent-notifier.ts:36, packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-wake.ts:135).
principle_conflict: P7: model identity changes verification semantics
Z1: trusts a model's assumed prior
Z3: trusts reasoning about the model
P4
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 verification strength is identical for every model; model-specific wording may only be tested in the measurement lane.

atoms.name: Two-way scope check: missing and excess
atoms.statement: A node's work must be verified in both directions, every owed deliverable present and nothing done beyond scope, with drive-by edits counted as defects.
atoms.mechanism: Stated only in the injected directive and the supervision doctrine (packages/senpi-task/src/completion/dag-verification-directive.ts:9, packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/SKILL.md:93); no code computes it.
atoms.proof_purpose: The final tree diff touches every declared deliverable path and no path outside the contract's declared write scope.
atoms.g1_design: The contract declares deliverables and write-scope globs; at completion G1 diffs the final tree against the contract's baseline tree and requires deliverables subset-of changed set and changed set subset-of scope (exact set checks, no LLM).

atoms.name: Typed contract fields replacing prose markers
atoms.statement: Every node prompt must carry TASK, DELIVERABLE, SCOPE (hard read/write bounds), VERIFY (literal command and expected result), and STOP WHEN with binary observables, but enforcement is a non-blocking regex lint.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine in packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/references/planning.md:131-150 and packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:98; dag-lint only warns when TASK: or STOP WHEN markers are missing and never rejects (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-lint.ts:2, :12-26).
principle_conflict: P8: prose markers prove nothing; only typed fields are checkable
atoms.proof_purpose: Every registered contract has a typed write scope, at least one executable check with a deterministic predicate, and an observable stop condition.
atoms.g1_design: Make deliverables, scope, checks (argv plus exit-code/output predicate), and stop condition typed fields of the G1 contract schema; registration is rejected when any is missing or a check is not executable.

atoms.name: Disjoint write scopes for parallel lanes
atoms.statement: Parallel lanes must have disjoint write scopes or be serialized, but this is prompt doctrine only; nothing in the engine declares or checks scopes.
atoms.mechanism: packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/references/planning.md:64 and packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:70 require disjoint scopes stated inside prompts; a repository-wide search finds only prompt text (for example packages/omo-senpi/src/components/todo-fanout-reminder/reminder.ts:5), no enforcement.
principle_conflict: P2: lane scheduling is native to agy; G1 may only gate tool calls
atoms.proof_purpose: Each lane wrote only inside its declared scope, and concurrently admitted lanes had pairwise-disjoint scopes.
atoms.g1_design: (a) GOVERN: each lane's contract declares write-scope globs; PreToolUse denies file-write calls outside the active lane's scope and denies admitting a lane whose scope intersects a running lane's scope. The Stop-time tree diff (OMO-14) stays the authority because shell writes bypass PreToolUse (OMO-29). Requires measuring whether agy hook stdin identifies the subagent (conversationId or workspace path).

atoms.name: Gate node joins waves with n+m edges
atoms.statement: Instead of n x m edges between consecutive waves, one review node depending on all producers gates the next wave, and every work-producing graph ends with a verification node.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine in packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/references/planning.md:30 and :152-159; dag-lint only warns when a graph with two or more nodes has no verification-shaped node (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-lint.ts:28-32).
atoms.proof_purpose: An integration-level check set passed on the combined result of all producer contracts before any downstream contract started.
atoms.g1_design: (b) BUILD at contract level: allow a gate contract that depends on all producer contracts and holds the integration checks; downstream contracts depend only on it, so admission (OMO-09) needs one receipt instead of n.

atoms.name: Same admission gate on every spawn path
atoms.statement: The DAG scheduler and recovery apply the same spawn policy (plan gate, prompt contract) as direct task spawns, so orchestration cannot bypass restrictions.
atoms.mechanism: DagNodeSpawnPolicy is evaluated once per admission before startOwned (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/scheduler.ts:81-94, :980-991) and wired from evaluateSpawnPolicy (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/index.ts:121-132, packages/senpi-task/src/tools/task/spawn-policy.ts:12-25); recovery receives the same policy (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery.ts:68).
atoms.proof_purpose: No subagent of any kind (single, teamwork lane, battle arm, auditor) started without passing G1's PreToolUse admission gate.
atoms.g1_design: (a) GOVERN: G1's PreToolUse matcher covers every agy spawn surface with one shared admission function; a host-contract E2E test asserts that each spawn path triggers a hook invocation.

atoms.name: Owner-keyed exactly-once execution with conflict detection
atoms.statement: Each node launch is keyed by an owner identity (run, node, fingerprint over definition, node, and execAttempt) under a lock: a match reuses the task, a live mismatch is a conflict, and a terminal mismatch starts fresh.
atoms.mechanism: startOwned takes an owner lock, consults findOwnedTask and ownedResult, and returns reused, owner_conflict, or a fresh launch (packages/senpi-task/src/manager/manager.ts:289-339); the owner fingerprint is keyed on execAttempt, never the display attempt (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/scheduler.ts:995-1010); a crash test keeps the spawn count at one (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/e2e-failure.test.ts:530).
atoms.proof_purpose: Each receipt is the unique result of one verification execution for an exact key (contract hash, check id, tree hash, env digest, attempt); a crash or re-entry never double-runs a check or substitutes a mismatched result.
atoms.g1_design: (b) BUILD in G1's own check runner: compute a verification key, lock it, reuse an existing receipt only on exact key match, wait for an in-flight one, and never substitute a different-key result; attempts increment only on deliberate re-verification.

atoms.name: Unchained JSONL WAL with checkpoint projection
atoms.statement: Events go to a per-run JSONL WAL with strictly increasing seq and fsync, checkpoints are temp+rename projections, torn tails are truncated, and unknown schemas fail closed, but entries are not hash-chained.
atoms.mechanism: appendEvent enforces seq = tail+1 and fsyncs (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/store.ts:164-180); the journal writes WAL before checkpoint and replays the tail on open (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/journal.ts:95-136, :177-195); only an incomplete last line is truncated (store.ts:465-501); schema mismatch is fatal (store.ts:572-579). The Codex loop publishes immutable revisions by hard link, also without a chain (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/plan-commit.ts:38-85).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 hash-chained append-only ledger with head anchor, pending journal, and crash recovery
principle_conflict: Z2: no hash chain or anchor, so anyone with file access can rewrite history undetected; weaker than T1
atoms.proof_purpose: none beyond T1
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT in favor of T1's chained ledger; optionally adopt the explicit rule 'an incomplete trailing line is truncated, a malformed complete line is fatal'.

atoms.name: Randomized SIGKILL crash test at durability boundaries
atoms.statement: A test SIGKILLs a writer process paused at a randomized mutation boundary and asserts the reopened store has a whole checkpoint, replays every journaled event, and leaves no temp files.
atoms.mechanism: The test spawns a script that appends N events, pauses after a randomized append and before the checkpoint write, kills it, then reopens and checks checkpointSeq, replay, and the absence of .tmp files (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/e2e-failure.test.ts:731-783).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 pending journal and crash recovery (the test method is new)
atoms.proof_purpose: The G1 ledger survives a kill at any append or head-anchor boundary, proven by test rather than argued.
atoms.g1_design: Add a G1 test that kills the ledger writer at every boundary (after entry write, after fsync, before and after head-anchor rename) in randomized order and asserts chain/head verification and no residue; run it for every ledger change.

atoms.name: Durable launch stamp before side effects
atoms.statement: A task's started_at is durable before the runner is invoked, recovery never auto-relaunches stamped-but-lost work (it folds as lost), and unstamped scheduled work is readmitted at most three times.
atoms.mechanism: Recovery readmits only lost tasks without started_at whose node is still scheduled and execAttempt < MAX_RECOVERY_READMISSIONS (3) (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery.ts:33-35, :344-361; packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:38).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 pending journal and crash recovery
atoms.proof_purpose: A verification whose launch was journaled but whose result never landed is recorded as interrupted and re-run in full; it is never assumed passed or silently skipped.
atoms.g1_design: G1 writes a pending 'verification launched' entry before executing a check; on recovery such an entry becomes 'interrupted' and the check re-runs under a new attempt, with automatic re-runs capped (T1 bounded loops).

atoms.name: Pid-liveness resume leases
atoms.statement: Paused runs are claimed with a pid lease checked by a signal-0 probe, with special handling for the host's own pid and a watcher that re-claims when the holder exits.
atoms.mechanism: claimPausedRun and holderStillLive (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery.ts:198-220), self-pid rule (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:53), lease watch polling (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery-lease-watch.ts:33), pid-based stale lock reclaim (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/store.ts:624).
principle_conflict: P7: agy hooks are short-lived sh -c processes, so a hook pid says nothing about an agent session
P1: pid liveness is not durable state
Z7: PID reuse makes liveness unproven
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 ownership is a ledger fact, not a process lease.

atoms.name: Session-owned runs strand work across sessions
atoms.statement: Runs belong absolutely to their parent session; any other session gets run_not_owned, and only an immediate fork of a session whose holder is proven dead may adopt a paused run.
atoms.mechanism: ownedRecord and the wait surface reject a foreign parentSessionId (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/manager.ts:261-271, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/handle.ts:104); recovery skips foreign sessions except fork adoption with proven abandonment (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery.ts:142-196).
principle_conflict: P1: a fresh agent in a new conversation must continue durable work; binding state to a session id strands it
P3: conversation identity is not state
TW(b)
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 state is owned by the workspace ledger; agy conversationId is recorded only as provenance.

atoms.name: Result-file presence implies completion on resume
atoms.statement: On recovery a completed node's result file is reused, and a scheduled or running node whose task vanished but whose result file exists is transitioned to completed.
atoms.mechanism: reconcileNodes reuses persisted outputs (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery.ts:261-273) and marks a taskless node completed when readDagNodeResult finds a file (recovery.ts:305-312); result artifacts carry sha256 and bytes (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/results.ts:62-97, :174-180).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding output digests
principle_conflict: Z5: a file in an agent-writable directory is presented evidence
P4: no re-verification on resume
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT as authority: on resume G1 trusts only ledger receipts whose digests verify against G1-owned storage; a stray result file completes nothing.

atoms.name: Pin injected guidance digests at contract creation
atoms.statement: Skills are resolved once at run creation into a manifest with each skill's name and sha256 plus the pinned cwd, and resumed runs read that manifest instead of the current SKILL.md files.
atoms.mechanism: createDagSkillMaterializer writes requested/resolved{name,sha256}/missing/prompt/effectivePrompt per node with the pinned cwd (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/skills.ts:14-37, :106-137); resume reads the manifest only (skills.ts:139-147); missing skills are diagnostics, not failures (skills.ts:101; packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:56).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant RULES.md situational index (adds digest pinning)
atoms.proof_purpose: The guidance G1 injects for a contract after any restart is byte-identical to what was pinned at contract creation, or the drift is recorded.
atoms.g1_design: At registration G1 stores the sha256 (and a copy) of every rule shard it will inject for the contract; SessionStart and PreInvocation inject the pinned copy and log any drift against the current shard files, keeping guidance outside the proof core (OMO-04).

atoms.name: Hard caps on graph size, active runs
atoms.statement: The engine caps nodes per run (64), dependency fan-out, prompt bytes (256 KiB), and active runs per session (16, terminal runs excluded), and prunes terminal runs after 7 days.
atoms.mechanism: DAG_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/types.ts:108-117); compile-time caps (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/graph.ts:168-226); active-run cap under a session lock (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/store.ts:383-408); retention deletes event logs, results, and keys (store.ts:279-300, :902-923).
principle_conflict: P3: time-based pruning deletes event logs and results, i.e. evidence
atoms.proof_purpose: Contract graphs and verification work are bounded, while evidence is never pruned.
atoms.g1_design: Adopt fixed caps on contract-graph size, dependency fan-out, and concurrently active contracts (deny registration beyond them); reject time-based pruning of ledger entries or receipts (archive or compact only with chained digests).

atoms.name: Durable-before-emit; authority and telemetry lanes separated
atoms.statement: Only sequenced, already-durable boundary events enter the ledger channel, while live activity telemetry is unsequenced, never journaled, and kept on a separate channel so it cannot corrupt replay.
atoms.mechanism: Boundary vs activity lanes and the separate DagActivityEvent type (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/types.ts:58-62, :299-319, :409-412); emission only after WAL append and checkpoint replace (docs/reference/mass-ulw-protocol.md:160-172); separate channels and per-seq dedupe in the bridge (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-rpc-bridge.ts:31-36, :94-101).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection (partial)
atoms.proof_purpose: Every authority fact G1 reports was durable before it was observed, and no statistic, vector, or telemetry value ever enters the authority ledger.
atoms.g1_design: Two physically separate stores: the chained authority ledger (contracts, receipts) and an unsequenced measurement log (pass/fail vectors, Hamming distances, timings, A/B data); injections may cite measurement data only as advisory text, matching the decided mathematics placement.

atoms.name: Canonicalized path guard; shell is no boundary
atoms.statement: A tool_call guard blocks file tools whose canonicalized target (lexical path and realpath from the nearest existing ancestor, including apply_patch directives) falls in denied roots, and explicitly treats bash string inspection as advisory because it is bypassable.
atoms.mechanism: extractTargetPaths and extractPatchDirectivePaths gather targets (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/memory/guard.ts:112-145); isForbiddenTarget checks lexical and canonical candidates (guard.ts:147-179, :181-196); bash only logs an advisory (guard.ts:13, :31-37); a host filesystem policy is used when the host offers one (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/memory/policy-guard.ts:8-11, :43-58).
atoms.proof_purpose: No file-tool write targeted G1-protected roots, and a Stop-time digest check proves those roots (including both hooks.json files) are unchanged regardless of shell activity.
atoms.g1_design: PreToolUse denies write-tool calls whose canonicalized path falls in G1-protected roots (~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, .agents/hooks.json, G1 state, pinned check files); because run_command can write anything, G1 also verifies those roots' digests at every Stop and SessionStart and treats a mismatch as tamper that denies completion.

atoms.name: Agent-writable harness state without protection
atoms.statement: Goals, criteria, and ledger live in agent-writable files under .omo/, protected only by the instruction that they are never hand-edited, with no hash chain and no write guard.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine only (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:59); revisions are plain JSON published by hard link without a digest chain (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/plan-commit.ts:38-95); the only blocking tool_call handler in omo-senpi is the memory guard (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/memory/guard.ts:66), which does not cover .omo state.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 hash-chained append-only ledger with head anchor
principle_conflict: Z1: the agent can rewrite its own progress
Z2: and its own evidence
P3
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 state is chained and anchored (T1) and guarded by OMO-29.

atoms.name: Agent-asserted pass/fail evidence records
atoms.statement: Criterion status (pass, fail, blocked) is whatever the agent passes to recordEvidence, validated only for non-empty text and the existence of cited artifact paths.
atoms.mechanism: recordEvidence sets criterion.status = args.status after nonEmptyEvidence and resolveEvidenceArtifacts (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/evidence.ts:52-99); artifacts are checked only with existsSync (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/evidence-artifacts.ts:15-45).
principle_conflict: Z4: status is self-reported
Z5: the existence of a file is not proof
P4: G1 must run the check itself
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 receipts come only from G1 executing the check.

atoms.name: Attestation schema validation mistaken for verification
atoms.statement: The final quality gate validates an agent-authored JSON (literal APPROVE, self-declared passCount >= totalCriteria, reviewer name allowlist, non-empty current-attempt artifacts) and treats a structurally valid document as passing.
atoms.mechanism: validateQualityGate requires literal values and checks counts taken from the input itself (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/quality-gate.ts:67-155); artifacts need only be non-empty files in the current attempt dir (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/quality-gate-artifacts.ts:58-73); checkpoint calls it for final completion (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/checkpoint.ts:203-217).
principle_conflict: Z4: every field is authored by the agent
Z5
P4
P5: binds no G1-produced receipt
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT as authority; attempt-scoped freshness is already covered by T1 receipt sequence binding.

atoms.name: Evidence kind must match criterion surface
atoms.statement: Each evidence surface accepts only compatible artifact kinds (cli/tmux -> transcript or log, http -> http-dump, browser/gui -> screenshot or image, data -> data-diff).
atoms.mechanism: COMPATIBLE_KINDS and artifactCompatible are checked for every surface-evidence row (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/quality-gate-artifacts.ts:14-56, packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/quality-gate.ts:157-192).
atoms.proof_purpose: Every acceptance criterion is covered by at least one deterministic check whose observation type can actually observe it (typed, not just non-zero, coverage-matrix rows).
atoms.g1_design: Extend the decided criteria x checks coverage matrix with a declared observation type per criterion and per check (exit-code, file-digest, http-status, data-diff); registration rejects a criterion whose only checks have an incompatible type.

atoms.name: Keyword regex as anti-weakening guard
atoms.statement: Agent-proposed criterion revisions are accepted unless their text matches a keyword regex (skip, bypass, weaken near test or verification), and revise_criterion may rewrite any criterion's scenario or expected evidence regardless of its status.
atoms.mechanism: weakens() is a two-regex keyword test (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/steering.ts:85-88) feeding validateUlwLoopSteeringProposal (steering.ts:109-123); validateCriterion only checks ids and that an update is present (steering.ts:150-158).
principle_conflict: Z1: trusts the agent's wording
Z3: keyword detection is not proof
P5: criteria change under an existing contract
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: criteria are immutable under a contract hash; changes create a new contract version (OMO-35, T1).

atoms.name: Structured atomic strengthen-only contract steering
atoms.statement: State changes come only from typed, evidence-backed proposals applied atomically (accepted whole or rejected with reasons, both ledgered), and natural-language steering never mutates state.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:184-198); applySteeringMutation clones and applies only accepted proposals, and rejected ones are ledgered as steering_rejected (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/steering.ts:160-171, :217-222).
atoms.proof_purpose: Every contract mutation in the ledger is a validated typed record, and in-place mutations can only strengthen (add criteria or checks); anything else creates a superseding contract version.
atoms.g1_design: G1 accepts contract change proposals only as typed records checked atomically; in-place acceptance is limited to monotone strengthening proven by set inclusion (old criteria subset-of new, old checks subset-of new); everything else is rejected or becomes a new version with empty receipts.

atoms.name: Fail-before/pass-after discriminating checks
atoms.statement: A criterion that cannot fail is not a criterion: bug fixes need the failing case captured before and the same case passing after, and existing tests must be green on unchanged code first.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine only (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/define-goal.md:44, :52; packages/prompts-core/prompts/ultrawork/gemini.md:227; packages/shared-skills/skills/ulw-execute/SKILL.md:236); no code runs checks against a baseline.
atoms.proof_purpose: Each change-required check discriminates: it fails (or yields a different output digest) on the contract's baseline tree and passes on the final tree, so a vacuous or always-green check cannot produce a completion receipt.
atoms.g1_design: At registration G1 runs every check in its scrubbed runner on the baseline tree and records a baseline receipt; criteria marked change-required are rejected if they already pass; completion needs a pass receipt on the final tree plus the recorded baseline fail (exact equality checks only).

atoms.name: Pinned verification surface: no edited tests
atoms.statement: The rules forbid editing a test green, adding skip/.only/xfail, or deleting failing tests, and reviewers hunt deletion-only or tautological tests, but nothing enforces it mechanically.
atoms.mechanism: packages/prompts-core/prompts/ultrawork/gemini.md:227 (never edit a test green), :246 (no skip/.only/xfail added), :306 (no test deletion); the gate-reviewer prompt looks for deletion-only and tautological tests (packages/senpi-task/src/agents/builtin/gate-reviewer.ts:23).
atoms.proof_purpose: The checks that produced a completion receipt are byte-identical to the checks pinned at contract registration (or were changed only through a new contract version).
atoms.g1_design: At registration G1 records sha256 of every file the checks depend on (tests, scripts, configs named in the contract); PreToolUse denies write tools on those paths for the contract's lifetime, and completion recomputes the digests (catching shell edits) and denies completion on any mismatch.

atoms.name: Evidence bound to tree hash; freeze
atoms.statement: Evidence is stamped with git HEAD^{tree}, stays valid across rebases that keep the tree identical, must be re-run rather than relabeled when the tree changes, and the final gate runs on a frozen tree.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine in packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:64 and packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:122, :159, :162, :206; the validator itself checks only attempt directories (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/quality-gate-artifacts.ts:58-73).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding current source and tree
atoms.proof_purpose: The receipt was produced on exactly the tree being completed.
atoms.g1_design: Already in T1: bind receipts to the tree hash (content, not commit), so an identical tree after rebase keeps receipts valid while any content change invalidates them.

atoms.name: Cleanup receipts: no residual QA processes
atoms.statement: A criterion cannot be recorded as passed while any QA-spawned process, tmux session, browser context, port, container, or temp path is alive, and evidence must carry a cleanup receipt.
atoms.mechanism: Doctrine (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:121, :216, :225; packages/shared-skills/skills/ulw-execute/SKILL.md:182); enforcement relies on the agent writing the receipt string.
atoms.proof_purpose: G1's own verification left no residual processes or listeners, checked by G1 rather than claimed.
atoms.g1_design: Already in T1 (process-tree reaping); record in each receipt a G1-computed residue check (runner process group empty, no new listening sockets owned by the runner).

atoms.name: Progress-keyed continuation budget and escalation
atoms.statement: Automatic continuations are capped (8 per user input, 2 Stop resumes per goal, 5 cycles per goal, 3 identical failures), the resume counter resets only when the durable ledger grew, and a blocker signature seen 3 times escalates to needs_user_decision.
atoms.mechanism: CONTINUATION_LIMIT and stale-signature skip (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ulw-execute-continuation/index.ts:11, :91-120); RESUME_CAP keyed to ledger line count with a .stuck marker (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/stop-resume-hook.ts:14, :86-103); blocker escalation (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/checkpoint.ts:91-115); caps (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:99).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 stagnation and oscillation detection plus bounded loops
principle_conflict: Z2: their progress signals (ledger line count, plan checkbox counts) are agent-writable
atoms.proof_purpose: A Stop continuation is spent only when the G1 pass/fail vector changed since the previous continuation.
atoms.g1_design: Key the Stop 'continue' budget to the G1 receipt vector (Hamming distance to goal, per the decided control lane), resetting only when a G1 receipt changed it, within agy's hard cap of 10 continues; never key it to agent-editable files.

atoms.name: Suppress continuation on abort or pressure
atoms.statement: Continuations are not injected after an aborted turn, a host retry, a refusal, an unfinished tool turn, or an aborted tool result, nor when the transcript shows context-pressure markers, and a user cancel is never auto-resumed.
atoms.mechanism: readAgentEndOutcome returns a blocking reason for aborted, host-retry, refusal, unfinished-turn, and aborted-tool-result (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ulw-execute-continuation/agent-end-eligibility.ts:44-66); transcript context-pressure markers silence the Stop hook (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/stop-resume-hook.ts:18-26, :166-174); cancel rule (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:226).
principle_conflict: Z6: honoring a user abort trusts the user channel; acceptable because stopping never grants completion
atoms.proof_purpose: A Stop continuation was never emitted after a user abort or into an overflowing context; the agent stops but the contract stays incomplete.
atoms.g1_design: Measure what agy's Stop stdin and transcript record for user interrupts, refusals, and compaction; if observable, G1's Stop hook prints nothing in those cases while the ledger keeps the contract open.

atoms.name: Structured BLOCKED escape that never completes
atoms.statement: The Stop continuation can be ended by a first-line blocker marker only if a non-empty reason follows, so a bare marker echoed from untrusted text cannot silence the guard.
atoms.mechanism: hasAllowedExternalBlockerMarker requires the exact marker on the first line (or after the ultrawork opener) and at least one following non-empty line (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-execute-continuation/src/codex-hook.ts:43-61); blocked requires a true impasse (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/define-goal.md:95).
principle_conflict: Z4: the marker is agent output; acceptable only because it can end continuation, never complete a contract
atoms.proof_purpose: none for completion; it bounds continuation spend while the contract stays open and records the declared blocker
atoms.g1_design: G1's Stop hook accepts a structured 'BLOCKED: <failing check id> <reason>' declaration, verifies the cited check id is failing in the ledger, stops continuing, and records the contract as blocked, never completed.

atoms.name: Agent-written receipt gate with fail-open cap
atoms.statement: A SubagentStop hook blocks worker agents until their last message names an EVIDENCE_RECORDED path inside .omo/evidence (realpath-contained, regular file, at least 40 characters, mtime after transcript birth), but lets the stop through after 3 attempts or on context pressure.
atoms.mechanism: runSubagentStopHook and getEvidenceFileFailure (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/lazycodex-executor-verify/src/codex-hook.ts:9-34, :74-100); MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/lazycodex-executor-verify/src/state.ts:5); escape hatches (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/lazycodex-executor-verify/AGENTS.md:11).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding receipt sequence and hash
principle_conflict: Z5: the evidence file is written by the agent; 40 characters and mtime are forgeable
P4: fail-open after 3 attempts turns missing proof into a pass
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT; lesson: after G1's continuation cap the agent may stop, but completion stays denied; receipts are produced by G1, never cited by the agent.

atoms.name: Self-declared completion tokens (repo-deprecated)
atoms.statement: The older loop ended when transcript text contained <promise>DONE</promise> (or an 'Agent: oracle' line with <promise>VERIFIED</promise>), inspecting assistant text directly; the repo has deprecated it.
atoms.mechanism: detectCompletionInTranscript scans assistant and text entries for the promise tag (packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/ralph-loop/completion-promise-detector.ts:52-90); isOracleVerified only pattern-matches an 'Agent:' line and the tag (packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/ralph-loop/oracle-verification-detector.ts:11-55); the directory is marked DEPRECATED (packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/ralph-loop/AGENTS.md:7).
principle_conflict: Z4: completion by an agent-emitted string that any model can print
P4
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT; supporting evidence for G1's stance (the repo itself retired token-based completion; agy measurements show Gemini says DONE after blocked calls).

atoms.name: Reviewer re-roll cap and receipt-first ordering
atoms.statement: Reviewer spawns are capped per (reviewer type, goal, attempt) to stop shopping for approval, and the gate reviewer cannot be spawned until the manual-QA artifact exists.
atoms.mechanism: consumeReviewSpawnBudget keys counts by agentType:goalId:attempt with default limit 3 (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/spawn-guard.ts:33, :169-186); missingGateArtifact denies gate-reviewer spawns until the attempt's manual-QA file is non-empty (spawn-guard.ts:83-94, :188-205).
principle_conflict: P8: auditor verdicts are outside G1's authority path, so the cap protects only measurement integrity
atoms.proof_purpose: All auditor verdicts for a contract attempt are in the ledger (count <= cap), so an approval cannot be obtained by silently re-rolling reviewers, and audits happen only after G1 receipts exist.
atoms.g1_design: (a) GOVERN agy's auditor agent if used: PreToolUse counts auditor invocations per contract attempt (deny beyond the cap) and admits the auditor only after G1 receipts exist; PostToolUse records every verdict hash; verdicts stay advisory.

atoms.name: Fail-closed spawn guard on bad input
atoms.statement: The spawn guard denies the spawn when the hook payload is invalid, the guard throws, or the session state lock cannot be taken.
atoms.mechanism: runSpawnGuardCli writes a deny on a null payload or exception (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/spawn-guard.ts:129-143) and on state-lock timeout (spawn-guard.ts:76-79).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection
atoms.proof_purpose: A spawn admitted by G1 passed a fully evaluated gate; any evaluation failure denied it.
atoms.g1_design: Already in T1; on agy emit an explicit deny JSON on internal error (a crash also blocks), never print {} by accident, never print allow.

atoms.name: Registered role and isolated context at spawn
atoms.statement: Spawns must name an explicitly registered agent_type (a role described in the message does not count), and children start without the parent's history unless deliberately required.
atoms.mechanism: spawnRoleDenial (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/spawn-role-guard.ts:18-28) is applied in applySpawnGuards (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/spawn-guard.ts:48-55); fork_context false is the default doctrine (packages/shared-skills/skills/ulw-execute/SKILL.md:31).
atoms.proof_purpose: Every admitted subagent ran an allowlisted profile, and audit-role subagents started without the worker's narrative.
atoms.g1_design: Measure agy invoke_subagent arguments (profile id, branch/share workspace, history inheritance); if exposed, PreToolUse requires an allowlisted profile and denies history sharing for audit roles.

atoms.name: Canonical reviewer prompt discards caller prose
atoms.statement: For the one-shot plan reviewer the harness replaces whatever the caller wrote with one canonical sentence naming a plan path selected from session-recorded references, and follow-up messages are refused.
atoms.mechanism: planReviewContractOutcome forces buildPlanReviewPrompt(path) and treats caller paths only as selectors over recorded references (packages/senpi-task/src/tools/task/plan-review-contract.ts:6-11, :45-63, :74-85); task_send is refused in every state (packages/senpi-task/src/agents/interaction-policy.ts:1-5, :19-23); docs (docs/guide/orchestration.md:134).
principle_conflict: P8: G1 does not use reviewer verdicts for completion, so this has no proof purpose unless an auditor is used for measurement
atoms.proof_purpose: The auditor's input contained only G1-selected references (contract id, receipt paths), never worker claims.
atoms.g1_design: If agy's auditor is used, PreToolUse 'overwrite' replaces its prompt with a canonical template carrying only the contract id and G1 receipt paths taken from the ledger, never interpolating agent text.

atoms.name: User-channel-only facts; injected text excluded
atoms.statement: Gate-arming facts come only from raw user input after stripping harness-injected blocks; model-initiated skill reads and extension-sourced input can never arm the gate, and a later phase forbids returning to an earlier one.
atoms.mechanism: Three trust-separated observation channels (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/skill-invocation-tracker.ts:5-21, :40-49); evaluateInvocationGuard applies forbidden-phase first, then user-only requirements (packages/senpi-task/src/agents/invocation-guard.ts:1-7, :32-34, :60-101).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel
principle_conflict: Z6: user instructions are also not fully trusted; restrict this channel to facts only the user can author (authorization, scope decisions)
atoms.proof_purpose: An authorization or decision fact in the ledger originated in a user-role transcript turn, not in agent output, tool results, or G1's own injected messages.
atoms.g1_design: G1 derives user-authored facts only from user-role entries of transcript_full.jsonl after removing G1's own injectSteps text (identified by a G1 nonce marker); model text and tool output can never create them.

atoms.name: Non-answer is not consent; scoped authorization
atoms.statement: Authorization questions are forced to required:true so a timed-out, dismissed, or unavailable answer refuses the gated action; approval authorizes only the named action class; and 'stop asking' never waives irreversible-decision authorization.
atoms.mechanism: question-gates sets required:true on ask_user_question/request_user_input calls whose header is Approval/Authorize/승인/권한 or whose option label starts with Approve/Authorize (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/question-gates/gate-rule.ts:5-48, packages/omo-senpi/src/components/question-gates/index.ts:24-31); tests show the no-answer result flips from 'continue' to refusal (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/question-gates/index.test.ts:251, :262); doctrine (packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/SKILL.md:27, packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-plan/SKILL.md:117-126).
principle_conflict: P6: G1 must not make the user operate G1; it may only enforce that a missing answer is never treated as authorization
atoms.proof_purpose: No contract-declared irreversible, spend, or scope action ran without a user-authored authorization fact for that exact action class.
atoms.g1_design: Measure agy's ask-user tool (timeout default, blocking flag); if it continues on timeout, PreToolUse 'overwrite' sets the blocking flag on authorization questions, and G1 denies contract-declared irreversible actions unless OMO-49 finds a matching user-authored authorization.

atoms.name: Contract quality bar with WHEN TO STOP
atoms.statement: A goal must state an outcome (never an activity), binary falsifiable criteria with scenario and evidence named before any edit, explicit in/out scope with recorded 'assumed:' constraints, and one binding WHEN TO STOP line.
atoms.mechanism: packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/define-goal.md:7-27 (quality bar and anatomy), :38-44 (criterion construction), :103 (criteria written after implementation is an anti-pattern); the same contract appears in the Gemini prompt (packages/prompts-core/prompts/ultrawork/gemini.md:210).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with a contract hash (adds stop expression and assumption fields)
atoms.proof_purpose: The contract names an observable stop state and every assumption it relies on, so a fresh agent can resume without the conversation.
atoms.g1_design: Add 'stop_when' (an expression over G1 receipts, such as all criteria passing) and 'assumed' (constraint, rationale, reversible) fields to the contract; registration rejects activity-only objectives without a checkable stop expression.

atoms.name: Native goal status is driver, never gate
atoms.statement: The host's native goal (create_goal/update_goal) is advisory steering only; the loop's own criteria gate completion, and native status never rejects or completes anything.
atoms.mechanism: packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:100-102; update_goal is allowed only after the loop's gate passes (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:204, :207).
atoms.proof_purpose: Completion state in G1 is never derived from agy's native task, goal, or subagent status.
atoms.g1_design: G1 ignores agy's native todo/goal/subagent status for authority; it may mirror G1 state into native surfaces one-way for UX.

atoms.name: Escape re-injected contract text as data
atoms.statement: When a stored objective is re-injected into a continuation prompt it is wrapped in <untrusted_objective> and XML-escaped, labeled as data rather than higher-priority instructions.
atoms.mechanism: buildContinuationPrompt and buildResumePrompt wrap and escape the objective (packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/goal/prompt.ts:3-11, :34-48).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel
atoms.proof_purpose: Text that G1 re-injects from agent- or user-authored contract fields cannot impersonate G1 directives.
atoms.g1_design: SessionStart and PreInvocation injections place contract text inside a G1-nonce-delimited, escaped data block, separate from G1's fixed directive text.

atoms.name: Re-read durable state, never memory
atoms.statement: Every automatic continuation tells the agent to read the plan and ledger first as the only sources of truth and not to trust its memory of prior turns.
atoms.mechanism: ulw-execute continuation directive (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ulw-execute-continuation/index.ts:206); after compaction re-read brief, goals, and ledger (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:61, packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:56).
atoms.proof_purpose: none beyond T1: resumption content comes from G1 state, not the conversation
atoms.g1_design: Already in T1; G1's SessionStart injection is generated from the ledger only.

atoms.name: Silence over stale or empty projections
atoms.statement: Projections stay silent while recovery runs or the store is unreadable, because publishing a pre-recovery or empty snapshot would be read as 'finished'.
atoms.mechanism: The RPC bridge attaches only after recovery ('dark beats lying') (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-runtime.ts:543-547); an unreadable store publishes nothing instead of an empty list (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-rpc-bridge.ts:77-90, :154-157).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection
atoms.proof_purpose: G1 never injects a state it could not verify (no false 'nothing active' or 'done').
atoms.g1_design: Already in T1: if ledger verification fails at SessionStart, inject nothing or an explicit 'G1 state unverifiable' marker, never a default or empty state.

atoms.name: Safe path segments for agent-derived ids
atoms.statement: Any id that becomes a path segment is validated against empty, '.', '..', separators, NUL, and ':', and the store additionally checks containment after joining.
atoms.mechanism: isSafeDagPathSegment (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/types.ts:8-23) is enforced by compileDag (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/graph.ts:181-191) and by store path builders with a post-join relative-path containment check (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/store.ts:322-339); the Stop hook refuses crafted goal ids that escape its state dir (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/stop-resume-hook.ts:92-94).
atoms.proof_purpose: No G1 read or write derived from agent-supplied identifiers can escape G1's state directory.
atoms.g1_design: Validate every contract, criterion, and check id with a strict allowlist regex and verify containment after path join and realpath before any G1 file access.

atoms.name: Contract-first: deny mutation before registration
atoms.statement: The Gemini prompt demands intent classification before any tool call and forbids implementation without an explicit request, and criteria written after implementation are an anti-pattern, but both rely on the model obeying.
atoms.mechanism: GEMINI_INTENT_GATE (packages/prompts-core/prompts/ultrawork/gemini.md:7-35); goal registration before implementation (gemini.md:210); anti-pattern table (packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/define-goal.md:103); the only code analog is phase monotonicity for plan reviewers (packages/senpi-task/src/agents/invocation-guard.ts:64-74).
principle_conflict: P2: must not cripple native read/explore behavior; only mutating tools are gated
atoms.proof_purpose: Every workspace mutation happened under an already-registered contract hash, so criteria could not be written after the work.
atoms.g1_design: While no active G1 contract exists, PreToolUse denies mutating tools (file writes, run_command outside an allowlisted read-only set) with a reason explaining how to register a contract; read and search tools get empty output (native behavior).

atoms.name: Adversarial class taxonomy for harness E2E
atoms.statement: Nine trigger-mapped adversarial classes (malformed input, prompt injection, cancel/resume, stale state, dirty worktree, hung commands, flaky tests, misleading success output, repeated interruptions) must be probed or marked not applicable with a reason.
atoms.mechanism: packages/shared-skills/skills/ulw-execute/SKILL.md:172, :240 and packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/references/full-workflow.md:88 (doctrine; the agent records the probes).
atoms.proof_purpose: G1's host-contract E2E suite covers each failure class that can fake or lose completion, especially misleading success output and repeated interruptions.
atoms.g1_design: Use the taxonomy as a checklist for G1's own E2E and host re-tests (false DONE after a blocked call, interrupt mid-verification, stale receipts after a tree change), measured with the ensemble/CI lane.

atoms.name: Transcript-mtime activity clock, report-only
atoms.statement: A running node's liveness is the mtime of its child's transcript log, surfaced as 'quiet for N minutes' after 10 minutes but never used to cancel or fail anything.
atoms.mechanism: readDagNodeActivityAt stats the task event log and treats every fault as 'no activity' (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/node-activity.ts:8-23); DAG_NODE_QUIET_AFTER_MS is a reporting threshold only (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/types.ts:203-205); quietNodesNotice states the observation without a verdict (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/task/dag-quiet-nodes.ts:9-21).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 stagnation and oscillation detection (as a measurement input)
atoms.proof_purpose: none in the authority path; a measurement-lane liveness signal for deciding whether a Stop continuation is worth spending
atoms.g1_design: Read agy's transcript_full.jsonl mtime and size at Stop as a measurement input (stall vs progress) alongside the receipt vector; never fail or complete a contract from it.

atoms.name: Steer or revive a node's live child
atoms.statement: send steers a running child in place or revives a finished resident child with its context, moving a failed node back to running, but is refused for completed or cancelled runs and for one-shot agents.
atoms.mechanism: sendToDagNode and foldSendOutcome map steering outcomes to steer, revive, queued, or typed refusals (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/node-send.ts:32-160); a revive journals dag.node.steered plus a transition to running, and a watcher persists the result before folding the new outcome (node-send.ts:102-112, :165-194).
principle_conflict: P2: steering and reviving subagents is native agy behavior; G1 must not rebuild it
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: (c) REJECT: G1 builds no steering verb; a steered or revived lane simply produces new work that needs new G1 receipts; only the rule that a completed contract cannot be revived is kept (OMO-07).

adoption_candidates: OMO-37: pin digests of check/test files at registration; PreToolUse deny plus Stop-time digest recheck blocks the cheapest cheat (editing, skipping, or deleting tests).
OMO-36: run every check on the baseline tree first; a check that cannot fail cannot complete a contract (fail-before/pass-after as exact receipts).
OMO-09: GOVERN agy's native subagents by denying a lane's spawn until its upstream contracts hold G1 receipts; no scheduler is rebuilt.
OMO-05: Merkle-style receipt keys over upstream receipt hashes make transitive invalidation of dependent contracts and checks self-verifying.
OMO-57: deny mutating tools until a contract hash exists, so criteria can never be written after the work.
OMO-14: exact set check of the tree diff against declared deliverables and write scope (nothing missing, nothing extra).
OMO-29: canonicalized PreToolUse guard for G1-protected roots plus Stop/SessionStart digest checks of both hooks.json files and G1 state, since shell writes bypass path guards.
OMO-16: per-lane write scopes enforced for parallel agy subagents (after measuring lane identity in hook stdin).
OMO-03: fold the G1 gate/verifier semantics digest into receipts so a G1 upgrade never reuses stale receipts.
OMO-01: deterministic contract-graph compile with cycle and unknown-dependency rejection at registration.
OMO-18: one admission gate covering every agy spawn surface (subagent, teamwork lane, battle arm, auditor).
OMO-19: exactly-once verification key (contract, check, tree, env, attempt) under a lock in G1's runner.
OMO-28: physically separate the authority ledger from measurement and telemetry streams (matches the decided mathematics placement).
OMO-35: accept in-place contract changes only when set inclusion proves they strengthen; everything else is a new version.
OMO-21: randomized SIGKILL crash test at every G1 ledger durability boundary.
risks: License: Sustainable Use License limits use to internal or non-commercial purposes; reuse ideas only and reimplement, do not copy code (LICENSE.md:10, LICENSE.md:26-28).

Auto-executing repo code: .claude/settings.json runs script/agent/setup.sh on SessionStart, which sources .env and runs bun install (network); .codex/setup.sh and .cursor/environment.json do the same, so never open this clone as an agent workspace (.claude/settings.json:3-9, script/agent/setup.sh:21, script/agent/setup.sh:58, .codex/setup.sh:9, .cursor/environment.json:2).
Telemetry is on by default and posts to PostHog (docs/guide/telemetry.md:3, packages/telemetry-core/src/constants.ts:1); recommended install is curl | bash (README.md:3).

Prompt-injection-style imperative text aimed at AI agents in repository instructions (AGENTS.md:3, AGENTS.md:11) and hook directives that tell the model its completion claim is a lie (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/lazycodex-executor-verify/directive.md:1); treated strictly as data in this analysis.

Completion authority is agent-authored: criterion status is self-reported (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/evidence.ts:76), the final quality gate validates agent-written JSON including a self-declared passCount (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/quality-gate.ts:97), and DAG node completion equals child status (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/scheduler.ts:888-899).

Fail-open escape hatches: the evidence-receipt Stop gate passes after 3 attempts or on context-pressure markers (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/lazycodex-executor-verify/AGENTS.md:11); the anti-weakening check is an evadable keyword regex (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-loop/src/steering.ts:85-88).

Write-scope disjointness and 'never hand-edit state' are prompt doctrine only (packages/omo-senpi/skills/mass-ulw/references/planning.md:64, packages/omo-senpi/skills/ulw-loop/SKILL.md:59); the repo itself states shell commands bypass its path guard (packages/omo-senpi/src/components/memory/guard.ts:31-37).

Agent-editable progress signals drive continuation: plan checkbox counts, including '[~]' blocked rows that leave the remaining count (packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ulw-execute-continuation/src/plan-checklist.ts:23-25, packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ulw-execute-continuation/index.ts:113).

Retention pruning deletes event logs and results of terminal runs after 7 days (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/store.ts:279-300, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/types.ts:115), which would violate P3 if copied.

Unsupported quantitative and model-specific claims: '95% confidence = ~60% actual' (packages/prompts-core/prompts/ultrawork/gemini.md:206); a weaker verification directive for one model justified only by a comment (packages/senpi-task/src/completion/dag-verification-directive.ts:13-15); approval-biased reviewers (packages/senpi-task/src/agents/builtin/gate-reviewer.ts:29, packages/omo-codex/plugin/components/ultrawork/agents/momus.toml:22).

Pid-liveness locks and leases assume a long-lived host process and are exposed to PID reuse (packages/senpi-task/src/dag/store.ts:591-642, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/recovery.ts:217-220); not transferable to agy's short-lived sh -c hooks.

Instability and scale: root AGENTS.md says the codebase is being rebuilt in a multi-harness refactor, the project is maintained by an AI assistant, and the DAG subsystem alone is about 14k LOC (AGENTS.md:3, README.md:16, packages/senpi-task/src/dag/AGENTS.md:3).
